questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding abdominal aorta aneurysms except :

options.label: A
options.text: Most favoured site for aneurysm generation by atherosclerotic region

options.label: B
options.text: More common in males and smokers

options.label: C
options.text: Most of these are asymptomatic and incidentally detected

options.label: D
options.text: Tendency of rupture does not correlate with the size of the aneurysm

questions.answerText: Tendency of rupture does not correlate with the size of the aneurysm
questions.solutionHtml:
Tendency of rupture does not correlate with the size of the aneurysm
  • Most cases of Abdominal Aorta Aneurysm (AAA) are asymptomatic and are discovered
  • incidentally on a physical exam as an abdominal mass.
  • AAAs occur more frequently in men and smokers, rarely developing before age 50.
  • Atherosclerosis is a major cause of AAA, but other factors contribute since the incidence is less than 5% in men older than age 60 years.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 504-507

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding inflammatory abdominal aorta aneurysms except :

options.label: A
options.text: Usually seen in old-age

options.label: B
options.text: Patient presents with back pain and elevated CRP

options.label: C
options.text: Histologically there is lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate and macrophages

options.label: D
options.text: Most of the patients don’t have associated inflammation of other arteries

questions.solutionHtml:
Usually seen in old-age
  • Inflammatory Abdominal Aorta Aneurysm accounts for 5% to 10% of all AAA; these typically occur in younger patients, who often present with back pain and elevated inflammatory markers (g.: elevation of C-reactive protein).
  • Inflammatory aneurysms are characterized by abundant lymphoplasmacytic inflammation with many macrophages (and even giant cells) associated with dense periaortic scarring that can extend into the anterior retroperitoneum.
  • The cause is a presumed localized immune response to the abdominal aortic wall; remarkably, most cases are not associated with inflammation of other arteries.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 504-507

questions.stem: Mutations in TGF-β receptors lead to defective synthesis of elastin and collagens I and III leading to aneurysms in which syndrome?

options.label: A
options.text: Marfan syndrome

options.label: B
options.text: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome

options.label: C
options.text: Loeys-Dietz syndrome

options.label: D
options.text: Churg strauss syndrome

questions.solutionHtml:
Loeys-Dietz syndrome
  • Loeys-Dietz syndrome is another cause of aneurysms; in this disorder, mutations in TGF-β receptors lead to defective synthesis of elastin and collagens I and III. Aneurysms in such individuals can rupture fairly easily (even at small sizes) and are thus considered to follow an “aggressive” course.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 505

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding mycotic aneurysms except:

options.label: A
options.text: Most common causative organism is a fungus

options.label: B
options.text: It can be a complication of infective endocarditis

options.label: C
options.text: It can be an extension of an adjacent suppurative process

options.label: D
options.text: Can originate from circulating organisms directly infecting the arterial wall

questions.answerText: Most common causative organism is a fungus
questions.solutionHtml:
Most common causative organism is a fungus
  • False, the most common pathogens are Staphylococcus aureus


Mycotic aneurysms can originate from:

  1. From embolization of a septic embolus, usually as a complication of infective endocarditis.
  2. As an extension of an adjacent suppurative process.
  3. By circulating organisms directly infecting the arterial wall.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 506

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding aortic dissection except:

options.label: A
options.text: Hypertension is the most common cause

options.label: B
options.text: Intimal tear is the initial event to occur

options.label: C
options.text: Absence of widening of the aortic silhouette on Chest X-Ray rules out Aortic dissection

options.label: D
options.text: Stanford type B requires medical management

questions.answerText: Absence of widening of the aortic silhouette on Chest X-Ray rules out Aortic dissection
questions.solutionHtml:
Absence of widening of the aortic silhouette on Chest X-Ray rules out Aortic dissection
  • False, While the widening of the aortic silhouette on Chest X-Ray increases the likelihood of Aortic Dissection, its absence does not reliably exclude the diagnosis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 507, 508

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding clinical features of aortic dissection except:

options.label: A
options.text: Presents with sudden onset of excruciating pain, usually beginning in the anterior chest, radiating to the back

options.label: B
options.text: It is classified into two types A and B, based on involvement Of ascending aorta

options.label: C
options.text: Most common cause of death is rupture of the dissection into the pericardial, pleural, or peritoneal cavities

options.label: D
options.text: Recognizable medial degeneration is a prerequisite for dissection and a reliable predictor of its occurrence

questions.answerText: Recognizable medial degeneration is a prerequisite for dissection and a reliable predictor of its occurrence
questions.solutionHtml:
Recognizable medial degeneration is a prerequisite for dissection and a reliable predictor of its occurrence
  • False, recognizable medial degeneration appears to be neither a prerequisite for dissection nor a reliable predictor of its occurrence.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 507, 508
